question: After receiving one opaque handover, does the relief seat have an irrevocable choice that guarantees exactly one parcel in both supplier states? Is that answer a property of the reference itself, or of what the team has agreed it means?
time_of_decision: One relief decision now, after one accepted sender handoff in the public role handler. Record relief GET /brief, /status and /inbox with ready true before the one POST /resolve. Stop without resolving is distinct. No waiting, guessing, timing, extra communication, sender-private view or privileged identifiers.
controlled_conditions: Two pinned native tasks: stock (committed, dropped) and in-flight (settles, fails). Never combine their role instructions.

When delivered, the same 32-hex token X denotes the original in one condition and an unused draft in another, by permuting the private identities. When no token arrives, compare explicit null and withheld original/draft with ready true. World owner sees the permutation, relief does not. Control cells are enumerations, not sampled or equiprobable trajectories.

For each identical complete relief-role view within a task, replay close, fresh, stop, and only if X was actually delivered, resume(X) and replace(X) where supported by that task. Freeze twice; score final parcels with the pinned native verifier. A rule is robust only if every compatible hidden case earns 1. Grades span a range, never an average over invented priors.
registered_predictions: With a delivered opaque X and no sender convention, no one-step relief rule guarantees one parcel in either task. The same delivered bytes can denote different private objects.

When the sender is guaranteed to hand over the original, resume(X) guarantees one parcel in stock and replace(X) guarantees it in-flight. This knowledge is a team convention, not a signal observable in X.
With no received reference and no supplied fate, neither one-step team has a guaranteed rule, even under the original-only convention. At least one action earns 1 in some states.
retained_data: Separately classify the 16 previously published in-flight native cuts: did the final decision follow a served reference, did the sender meet this convention, and is the chosen action grade within the verified range? Missing rows, missing prior receipts, post-decision receipts, native failures, and no decision stay separate. Do not count a late/absent reference as a receipt or successful verification as intent. This is retrospective, not an independent replication.
pass: All predicted guarantee sets match exact scores across indistinguishable views; each analyzed native decision falls within its appropriate grade set and no unavailable reference is treated as delivered. Publish deviations.
limits: role handler and native ledger grading, not a new seat or transport trial
one irreversible move, not a bound on all multi-turn team protocols
public cuts are retained producer claims, not proof that a model perceived a message
